mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in UNRATE below 4.0% for two consecutive months signals weakening labor demand, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in GDPC1 for three consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for three consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly below zero in at least 70% of triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in INDPRO above 0.5% for four consecutive months signals accelerating industrial production, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly above zero in at least 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in FEDFUNDS and a fall in CPIAUCSL by more than 0.2% in the same month signals a restrictive monetary policy with declining inflation, which typically supports stable growth and positive equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases AND CPIAUCSL decreases by >0.2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly above zero in at least 55% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST for two months indicates deteriorating housing and overall demand, which reduces consumer spending and equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline in two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in PAYEMS above 160,000 for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly above zero in at least 65% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on negative relationship exists between RSAFS and S&P 500 5-day returns: higher household savings (RSAFS) coincide with lower near-term equity returns as consumers defer spending.
failure_condition: No significant negative correlation between RSAFS changes and S&P 500 5-day returns over a 5-year rolling window.
